stage_b_review_note: At line 6683 the source assumes surjective f between locally Noetherian schemes and EITHER syntomic, flat lci, or finite-type Gorenstein; it asserts K dualizing on Y iff Lf^*K dualizing on X. The draft retains all three disjunctive sufficient conditions and both directions without adding properness.
statement: For a locally Noetherian scheme $T$, *Cohen–Macaulay* means that every local ring $\mathcal O_{T,t}$ has depth equal to Krull dimension. A complex $D_T\in D(\mathcal O_T)$ is *dualizing* if affine locally it is represented by a bounded coherent complex of finite injective dimension with the self-duality isomorphism $A\simeq R\operatorname{Hom}_A(D,D)$. For a flat finite-presentation morphism $f:X\to Y$, *Cohen–Macaulay at $x$* means the local ring of the fibre $X_{f(x)}$ at $x$ is Cohen–Macaulay. A *Gorenstein local ring* is a Noetherian local ring of finite injective dimension as a module over itself; a scheme $T$ is *Gorenstein* if it is locally Noetherian and all its local rings are Gorenstein. A complex in $D(\mathcal O_T)$ is *derived-invertible* if it has a two-sided derived tensor inverse, equivalently it is locally a shift of a line bundle. For a scheme morphism $f:X\to Y$ whose fibres are locally Noetherian, *Gorenstein at $x$* means that $f$ is flat at $x$ and the local ring of $X_{f(x)}$ at $x$ is Gorenstein; *Gorenstein morphism* means this condition at every point. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a surjective morphism of locally Noetherian schemes satisfying at least one of: (i) $f$ syntomic (flat lfp lci); (ii) $f$ flat and a local complete intersection; (iii) $f$ a finite-type Gorenstein morphism (flat with Gorenstein fibres). For any $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)$, the complex $K$ is dualizing on $Y$ iff its derived pullback $Lf^*K$ is dualizing on $X$. The assertion includes both ascent and descent; no properness of $f$ is imposed.
hypotheses: f surjective locally Noetherian, syntomic or flat lci or finite-type Gorenstein; K in D_QCoh(Y).
conclusions: Dualizing complex condition ascends and descends under these covers.
